Introduction:
University of Hawaiʻi Mānoa
Consent to Participate in a Research Project
Title: Sustaining Crane Conservation Through Farmer Participation


Hello! You are being asked to take part in a research study about your preferences for participating in crane conservation as part of an investigation conducted by the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. You are eligible for this study if you are a rice farmer and you are at least 18 years old.


Objectives: The goal of this research is to understand farmers' preferences for participation in crane-friendly rice farming programs in Cambodia. You will be asked to respond to hypothetical (potential) conservation program scenarios that vary in features such as training opportunities, fertilizer support, participation requirements, and financial incentives. This information will help design conservation programs that work better for farmers.


Project Description – Activities and Time Commitment: If you decide to take part, you will be asked to complete a survey. Most questions are multiple choice, with a few questions asking for your opinion. The survey includes several hypothetical choice scenarios and questions about your farming experience. Completing the survey will take approximately 10-12 minutes. We expect approximately 100 farmers will take part in this study.


Benefits and Risks: There is no direct benefit to you for taking part in this project. We hope the information collected will help improve conservation programs for crane-friendly rice farming in Cambodia. There is little risk associated with participating in this study.


Confidentiality and Privacy: This study collects no personal identifying information. You will remain anonymous. The records from this study are kept private and only UH researchers will have access to them. Please do not include any personal information in your survey responses.


Voluntary Participation: You can freely choose to take part or not take part in this survey. There will be no penalty or loss of benefits for either decision. 

If you agree to participate, you can stop at any time.
Questions: If you have questions about this study, please contact Kirsten Oleson at 808-956-8864 or koleson@hawaii.edu. You may contact the UH Human Studies Program at 808-956-5007 or uhirb@hawaii.edu to discuss problems, concerns, or questions, or to offer input from someone unaffiliated with this research.


Please visit https://www.hawaii.edu/researchcompliance/information-research-participants for more information on your rights as a research participant.
